about: neFaRec's guide to common gym equipment. Each id matches a label of the on-device equipment model. 'labels' are words printed on the machine itself that the scanner looks for; 'exercises' are library ids, most useful first. 'image' is a public-domain photo from free-exercise-db of someone using it.

equipment.name: Leg press
equipment.what: You push a weighted platform away with your legs. A safe way to train your thighs heavy without balancing a bar.
setup: Sit with your back and hips flat against the pad.
Put your feet flat in the middle of the platform, about shoulder-width apart.
Push the platform up a little, then swing the safety handles out before you start.
equipment.tip: Lower until your knees come towards your chest, as long as your lower back stays on the pad.
equipment.mistake: Locking your knees straight at the top. Keep a slight bend.

equipment.name: Leg extension
equipment.what: You sit and straighten your legs against a padded bar. It works the front of your thighs on their own.
setup: Line your knees up with the machine's pivot, the round joint beside the seat.
Set the ankle pad so it rests on the front of your shins, just above your feet.
Sit back against the pad and hold the handles.
equipment.tip: Lift for a count of one and lower for a count of two. A light weight is plenty.
equipment.mistake: Swinging the weight up and letting it crash back down.

equipment.name: Leg curl
equipment.what: You bend your knees against a padded bar. It works the back of your thighs. Some you lie on, some you sit in.
setup: Line your knees up with the machine's pivot.
Set the pad so it rests on the back of your lower legs, just above your heels.
On the seated version, bring the thigh pad down so it holds your legs in place.
equipment.tip: Curl all the way, then lower slowly.
equipment.mistake: Lifting your hips off the pad to move more weight.

equipment.name: Lat pulldown
equipment.what: You sit and pull a bar down from overhead. It builds the muscles you'd use for a pull-up.
setup: Set the knee pad so your thighs are locked in when you sit.
Stand to grab the bar a little wider than your shoulders, then sit down with it.
Lean back slightly and keep your chest up.
equipment.tip: Pull the bar to your upper chest, leading with your elbows.
equipment.mistake: Pulling the bar behind your neck, or leaning far back to yank it down.

equipment.name: Seated row
equipment.what: You sit and pull handles towards your stomach. It works the middle of your back and helps your posture.
setup: Sit with your feet on the footplate and your knees slightly bent.
Grab the handle with straight arms and sit up tall.
If there's a chest pad, set it so you just reach the handles with straight arms.
equipment.tip: Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of each pull.
equipment.mistake: Rocking your whole body back and forth to move the weight.

equipment.name: Chest press
equipment.what: You sit and push handles away from your chest. Like a bench press, but the machine keeps the path steady.
setup: Set the seat so the handles are level with the middle of your chest.
Sit back with your shoulder blades against the pad.
Some machines have a foot lever that brings the handles forward to start.
equipment.tip: Push out, then let the handles come back until you feel a stretch across your chest.
equipment.mistake: Setting the seat so low that the handles sit up at your shoulders.

equipment.name: Shoulder press
equipment.what: You sit and push handles up overhead. It builds your shoulders without balancing dumbbells.
setup: Set the seat so the handles start just above your shoulders.
Sit with your back flat against the pad.
Hold the handles with your wrists straight.
equipment.tip: Press up without slamming your elbows straight at the top.
equipment.mistake: Arching your lower back off the pad.

equipment.name: Pec deck
equipment.what: You bring two arms or handles together in front of you. Facing the other way, it works the back of your shoulders.
setup: Set the seat so the handles are at chest height.
For your chest, sit with your back on the pad and bring the handles together in front of you.
For the back of your shoulders, face the pad and push the handles back and out.
equipment.tip: Keep a soft bend in your elbows the whole time.
equipment.mistake: Going so heavy that your shoulders roll forward.

equipment.name: Smith machine
equipment.what: A barbell that slides up and down on fixed rails. Good for learning squats and presses, because the bar can't drift forward or back.
setup: Twist the bar to unhook it from the hooks, and twist back to rack it.
Set the safety stoppers just below the lowest point of your lift.
Put the bench or your feet in place first, then unhook the bar.
equipment.tip: Start with the empty bar. On many Smith machines it weighs less than a normal 20 kg bar.
equipment.mistake: Skipping the safety stoppers.

equipment.name: Hack squat
equipment.what: You squat with your back against a sliding pad. It works your thighs hard while the machine keeps you steady.
setup: Stand with your back and shoulders against the pads.
Put your feet in the middle of the platform, about shoulder-width apart.
Push up a little and release the safety handles before you lower.
equipment.tip: Go down until your thighs are about level with the platform, if your knees feel fine.
equipment.mistake: Letting your heels lift off the platform.

equipment.name: Cable station
equipment.what: Weight stacks with pulleys you can slide up or down. One machine for dozens of exercises.
setup: Pull the pin on the column to move each pulley up or down.
Clip on a handle, rope or bar.
Choose the weight with the pin in the stack.
equipment.tip: Cables keep the muscle working the whole way, so light weights feel harder than you expect.
equipment.mistake: Letting the weight stack slam down between reps.

equipment.name: Triceps pushdown
equipment.what: A cable from a high pulley that you push down to straighten your arms. It works the back of your upper arms.
setup: Clip a rope or short bar to the top pulley.
Stand close, with your elbows tucked into your sides.
Choose a weight you can push down 10 times without leaning over it.
equipment.tip: Only your forearms move. Your elbows stay pinned to your sides.
equipment.mistake: Leaning over the bar and pushing with your bodyweight.

equipment.name: Calf raise machine
equipment.what: You push up onto your toes against a weight. It works your calves.
setup: Stand or sit with the balls of your feet on the edge of the step.
Set the shoulder or knee pads so they press on you before you lift.
Let your heels drop below the step to start.
equipment.tip: Pause for a second at the top and at the bottom.
equipment.mistake: Bouncing through quick, short reps.

equipment.name: Hip abduction machine
equipment.what: You push your knees apart, or squeeze them together, against pads. Out works the side of your hips; in works your inner thighs.
setup: Sit with your back against the pad and your knees against the knee pads.
Pads on the outside of your knees: push out. Pads on the inside: squeeze in.
Many machines switch between the two with a lever or by flipping the pads.
equipment.tip: Move slowly and hold the widest point for a second.
equipment.mistake: Flinging the pads open with momentum.

equipment.name: Ab crunch machine
equipment.what: You curl forward against a weight. It works your stomach muscles.
setup: Set the seat so the chest pad or handles sit at your upper chest.
Hook your feet under the rollers, if there are any.
Hold the handles lightly. Your abs should do the work.
equipment.tip: Curl your ribs towards your hips, then come back up slowly.
equipment.mistake: Pulling the weight with your arms.

equipment.name: Back extension bench
equipment.what: You hinge forward over a pad and lift your body back up. It works your lower back and glutes.
setup: Set the pad so it sits just below your hip bones.
Hook your heels under the foot pads.
Cross your arms over your chest to start.
equipment.tip: Come up until your body is in a straight line, and no higher.
equipment.mistake: Arching back hard past straight.

equipment.name: Dip machine
equipment.what: You push handles down beside you to straighten your arms. It works your triceps and chest. On assisted ones, the weight helps lift you.
setup: Set the seat so the handles start at about chest height.
On an assisted dip machine, more weight on the stack means more help.
Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.
equipment.tip: Lower until your elbows reach about a right angle.
equipment.mistake: Shrugging your shoulders up as you push.

equipment.name: Dip station
equipment.what: Two parallel bars you hold yourself up on. Use them for dips, or hang your legs for knee and leg raises.
setup: Grab the bars and jump or step up to straight arms.
Cross your feet behind you.
Lean forward a little to work your chest, or stay upright for your triceps.
equipment.tip: Too hard for now? Start with bench dips, or knee raises on the bars.
equipment.mistake: Dropping too deep and straining your shoulders.

equipment.name: Preacher curl bench
equipment.what: An angled pad your upper arms rest on while you curl. It keeps your body out of it so your biceps do all the work.
setup: Set the seat so your armpits sit on top of the pad.
Rest the backs of your upper arms flat on the pad.
Use an EZ bar or a dumbbell.
equipment.tip: Lower slowly until your arms are nearly straight.
equipment.mistake: Lifting your elbows off the pad.

equipment.name: Weight bench
equipment.what: A padded bench for pressing, rowing and seated work. Adjustable ones tilt up for incline exercises.
setup: Pull the pin or lever under the back pad to change the angle.
Keep it flat for presses and rows, or tilt it up for incline work.
Check the pin has clicked in before you sit down.
equipment.tip: Plant your feet flat on the floor when you press.
equipment.mistake: Training on a back pad that hasn't locked in place.

equipment.name: Dumbbells
equipment.what: A short handle with a weight on each end, one for each hand. The most useful thing in the gym for a beginner.
setup: Lift them off the rack with a flat back, the way you'd lift a box.
Start lighter than you think. You can always go up next set.
Put them back on the rack in order when you're done.
equipment.tip: Use the same weight in both hands so you can see if one side is weaker.
equipment.mistake: Dropping them from height at the end of a set.

equipment.name: Barbell
equipment.what: A long bar you load with plates. It's what squats, deadlifts and the bench press are done with.
setup: A standard long bar weighs 20 kg on its own.
Load the same plates on both sides and put a collar on each end.
For squats and the bench press, set the rack's safety bars first.
equipment.tip: Learn each lift with just the bar before you add plates.
equipment.mistake: Loading uneven plates, or skipping the collars.

equipment.name: Weight plates
equipment.what: The discs you load onto bars and plate-loaded machines. The number on each one is its weight.
setup: Check whether the number is in kg or lb. It's usually printed next to it.
Load the heaviest plates on first, then the lighter ones.
Carry them with both hands, by the edges or the handle holes.
equipment.tip: To know what you lifted, add both sides and the bar: a 20 kg bar with a 10 kg plate each side is 40 kg.
equipment.mistake: Leaving your plates on the bar or machine when you finish.

equipment.name: Treadmill
equipment.what: A moving belt you walk or run on. Good for warming up, or for steady cardio.
setup: Clip the safety key to your clothes. If you slip, the belt stops.
Stand on the side rails, press start, and step on once the belt is moving slowly.
Raise the speed a little at a time.
equipment.tip: A brisk walk with some incline makes a good warm-up or finisher.
equipment.mistake: Holding on to the handrails the whole time.

equipment.name: Exercise bike
equipment.what: A bike that doesn't go anywhere. Easy on your knees, so it's a good first piece of cardio.
setup: Stand next to it and set the seat to about hip height.
At the bottom of each pedal stroke your knee should still be slightly bent.
Strap your feet into the pedals.
equipment.tip: Turn the resistance up until it feels like riding up a gentle hill.
equipment.mistake: Riding with the seat too low, which strains your knees.

equipment.name: Rowing machine
equipment.what: You slide back and forth pulling a handle, like rowing a boat. It works almost your whole body.
setup: Strap your feet in so the strap crosses the widest part of your foot.
Hold the handle with straight arms and bent knees.
Push with your legs first, then lean back slightly, then pull with your arms.
equipment.tip: Legs, body, arms on the way back. Arms, body, legs on the way in.
equipment.mistake: Pulling with your arms before your legs have pushed.

equipment.name: Stair climber
equipment.what: Moving stairs that never end. Tough cardio that also works your legs.
setup: Hold the rails lightly for balance, not to carry your weight.
Start at a slow level for the first few minutes.
Stand tall and take full steps.
equipment.tip: Ten minutes at a steady pace is a solid warm-up.
equipment.mistake: Leaning on the rails so your legs do less.
